summary: A humorous introduction to WhimsyWidgets Inc.'s Remote Work Expense and Reimbursement Policies, explaining what home-office costs employees can and cannot expense. It covers furniture, receipts, internet, office supplies, snacks, electricity, and a miscellaneous clause, all in a joking tone. The closing urges employees to keep expenses necessary, legitimate, and within reason, and to direct questions to the Finance Department.
one_line: WhimsyWidgets Inc.'s tongue-in-cheek remote work expense policy covering furniture, receipts, internet, supplies, snacks, electricity, and miscellaneous items.
key_facts: WhimsyWidgets Inc. calls its policy document the Remote Work Expense and Reimbursement Policies.
The company will not reimburse a pet hamster's "consulting hours" for staring at an employee's screen.
Furniture, such as a massaging, coffee-brewing office chair, may only be expensed if it contributes to actual work; a chair that turns into a spaceship should stay on a personal wishlist.
Employees must keep receipts for all expenses, including items like sticky notes or an ergonomic mouse; a fake receipt from 'Le Fancy Schmancy' that looks like a dog's drawing would prompt a chat.
Internet bills that look like they are meant for a server farm or small country should be flagged by email, and Netflix premium charges should not be included in attachments.
Office supplies are for office work only; the policy mocks the legend of "Sir Prints-a-lot" and a paper mache castle built from supplies.
Snacks are self-funded (BYOSnacks) unless the employee is hosting a team munch-fest over Zoom; "testing the camera's food filter" is not an acceptable reason to expense a pizza.
Electricity expensed at a level that could power a small concert stage would raise suspicion of a side gig as a disco operator.
The Miscellaneous Mayhem Clause says quirky items may be approved if they make the company laugh and don't bankrupt it, such as a clown nose to "focus during meetings"; approval is not promised.
The company encourages employees to be mindful and responsible, keeping expenses necessary, legit, and not making accountants cry.
Questions or laughable submissions go to the Finance Department, jokingly called the Reimbursement Comedy Club.
A P.S. states that a "Fido's Feng Shui consultant" falls under 'Nope'.
